newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market recommended in Forbes magazine.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market recommended in Forbes magazine.

text.p: - The New Zealand sharemarket has been tipped by a United States academic in the latest issue of Forbes magazine as "loaded with value" and likely to substantially rally by early next year, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.

Steve Hanke, professor of applied economics at The Johns Hopkins University, singled out the following stocks in the magazine's money and investments column - DB Group, Lane Walker Rudkin Industries, St Lukes Group, Kiwi Income Property Trust, Air New Zealand B shares, PDL Holdings and Fisher and Paykel Industries.
In an article titled "value downunder," he said that New Zealand's economic fundamentals were superb.

He said the New Zealand market was undervalued with a price-earnings ratio of 13.5, a book-to-market ratio of 0.6 and a dividend yield of 4.7 percent compared with 17.6, 0.2 and 2.2 percent respectively for the US market.
Hanke argued that value stocks outperformed glamour stocks.
"There's a lesson here. It is that old expectations die hard. People expect great things of the growth stocks, and when at first they don't deliver, the believers continue to believe.
"It's the reverse for the value stocks: Not expecting much from them, analysts typically under-predict their earnings," Hanke said.
He said most money managers have historically overweighted their portfolios toward glamour stocks and they have typically underperformed the overall market over the last 25 to 30 years.

"Which brings me to my favourite value. Its not a stock but a whole market, one currently out of favour with good prospect for pleasant surprises. I'm talking about New Zealand," he said. Hanke, who has written in the magazine previously praising New Zealand, said that the markets were worried about New Zealand First party leader Winston Peters.
"In my view, Peters is a long shot to become Prime Minister after next month's (October's) general election. He will fade into the sunset as did Patrick Buchanan here," he said.
He said the New Zealand sharemarket had also been held back by a negative yield curve which would become positive in the first half of 1997.
"The New Zealand market is loaded with value. Look for a substantial rally there by early next year." -- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746
